{{Short description|Whole-building energy simulation program}}
[[EnergyPlus]]<ref name="Energy+"/> is a whole-building energy simulation program that [[engineer]]s, [[architect]]s, and [[research]]ers use to model both energy consumption — for heating, cooling, ventilation, lighting, and  process and [[plug load]]s — and water use in buildings. Its development is funded by the [[U.S. Department of Energy]] Building Technologies Office.<ref name="Energy+">{{cite web|title=energy plus software|url=https://energyplus.net/|website=Energy plus|accessdate=17 June 2016}}</ref> EnergyPlus is a console-based program that reads input and writes output to text files. Several comprehensive graphical interfaces for EnergyPlus are also available.

==Main features==
*Integrated, simultaneous solution<ref name="Energy+"/> of thermal zone conditions and [[HVAC]] system response that does not assume that the [[HVAC]] system can meet zone loads and can simulate un-conditioned and under-conditioned spaces.
*Sub-hourly, user-definable time steps<ref name="Energy+"/> for interaction between thermal zones and the environment; with automatically varied time steps for interactions between thermal zones and [[HVAC]] systems 
*Heat balance-based solution<ref name="Energy+"/> of [[Thermal radiation|radiant]] and [[convective]] effects that produce surface temperatures thermal comfort and condensation calculations
*Atmospheric pollutant calculations<ref name="Energy+"/>
*[[Anisotropic]] sky model<ref name="Energy+"/> 
*Combined heat and mass transfer model<ref name="Energy+"/> that accounts for air movement between zones.
*[[Heat transfer]] model<ref name="Energy+"/>
*Simulation based on climate zone<ref name="Energy+"/>
*Advanced [[fenestration (architecture)|fenestration]] models<ref name="Energy+"/> including controllable window blinds, [[electrochromic]] glazings, and layer-by-layer heat balances that calculate solar energy absorbed by window panes.
*Component-based [[HVAC]]<ref name="Energy+"/> that supports both standard and novel system configurations.

===Stand-alone vs coupled simulation===
EnergyPlus is normally used as a stand-alone command-line application or together with one of many free or commercial GUIs. However, EnergyPlus can be linked with other applications to simulate more advanced numerical models. One method is '''BCVTB'''<ref>BCVTB: https://simulationresearch.lbl.gov/bcvtb</ref> (''Building Controls Virtual Test Bed''), which allows users to couple different simulation programs for co-simulation, and to couple simulation programs with actual hardware. For example, the BCVTB can simulate a building in EnergyPlus and the HVAC and control system in Modelica, exchanging data between them as they simulate. Programs that can be linked to BCVTB include [[EnergyPlus]], [[Modelica]] ([[OpenModelica]] or Dymola), [[Functional Mock-up Units]], [[MATLAB]], and [[Simulink]], [[Radiance (software)|Radiance]] for [[Ray tracing (physics)|ray-tracing]], [[ESP-r]], [[TRNSYS]], [[BACnet]] stack.

==Applications for sensitivity analysis with EnergyPlus==
There exist many software tools that can automate sensitivity analysis to various degrees. Here is a non-exhaustive list. Most of these tools have multiple options, including one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis, multidimensional discrete parametric, continuous low-discrepancy distributions, and pareto-front optimization (listed alphabetically):

* '''EnergyPlus''' parametric IDF objects.<ref>Parametric IDF objects: https://bigladdersoftware.com/epx/docs/8-5/input-output-reference/parametric-objects.html#parametric-objects</ref> This simple method is limited to discrete parametric analysis, using the auxiliary ParametricPreprocessor program that is bundled with EnergyPlus.
* '''EPlusR'''<ref>EPlusR: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/eplusr/vignettes/eplusr.html</ref> (''EnergyPlus R''): A research-level scripting toolkit for EnergyPlus in [[R (programming language)]].
* '''EpXL'''<ref>EpXL: https://github.com/SchildCode/EpXL/</ref> (''EnergyPlus Excel''): A simple Excel spreadsheet application with options for sensitivity/parametric analysis and pareto-front optimization.
* '''GenOpt'''<ref>GenOpt: https://simulationresearch.lbl.gov/GO/</ref> (''Generic Optimization Program''), optionally with the free GenOpt GUI ExcalibBEM<ref>ExcalibBEM: https://www.simeb.ca/ExCalibBEM/index_en.php</ref>
* {{proper name|'''jEPlus'''}}<ref>jEPlus: http://www.jeplus.org/wiki/doku.php</ref> (''Jython EnergyPlus''): A simulation manager for parametric analysis with EnergyPlus.
* '''OpenStudio''' Analysis Framework and Spreadsheet:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://github.com/NREL/OpenStudio-analysis-spreadsheet|title = Analysis Examples| website=[[GitHub]] |date = 29 August 2021}}</ref> A front-end for the OpenStudio Server, allowing for users to create large-scale cloud analyses using OpenStudio measures.
* '''SALib''':<ref>SALib: https://salib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/basics.html</ref> A Python library for general sensitivity analysis, which can be used with user-defined scripts to run EnergyPlus and extract results.
